blocks.text: Grasslands

The western basalt plains grasslands are one of Australia's most threatened ecosystems. Iramoo Wildflower Grassland is a remnant of this ancient landscape — a living archive of plants, soils and stories that have shaped this Country for millennia.
The GREEN Lab has strong links to the three grasslands managed by the Cairnlea Conservation Reserves Committee of Management:

Iramoo Wildflower Grassland Reserve 
Featherheads Wildflower Grassland 
Pimelea Wildflower Grassland

Kangaroo Grass (Themeda triandra)
Spiny Rice-flower (Pimelea spinescens)
Button Wrinklewort (Rutidosis leptorrhynchoides)
Matted Flax-lily (Dianella amoena)
Golden Sun Moth (Synemon plana)

blocks.text: Research
Our research bridges Indigenous knowledge and Western science to better understand, restore and care for native grassland ecosystems.
Current projects

Active investigations into seed germination, soil microbiology, fire ecology and the role of cultural burning in grassland regeneration. Projects run in partnership with Moondani Balluk and the Institute for Sustainable and Liveable Cities.

Cultural fire and grassland renewal
Native seed banking and germination
Grassland soil health
Climate resilience of remnant ecosystems
Education
We host school groups, university classes and community workshops on the grassland — learning by walking, looking, and listening to Country.
Programs
Curriculum-aligned excursions for primary and secondary schools. Tertiary field studies in ecology, restoration and Indigenous land management. Open days and workshops for the public.

Guided grassland walks
Seasonal wildflower identification sessions
Teacher professional development
University field placements
Engagement
GREEN Lab is a meeting place. We work with community groups, traditional custodians, councils and volunteers to care for the grasslands together.
Get involved
Volunteer days run year-round — weeding, seed collection, monitoring and planting. No experience needed. Tools, gloves and morning tea provided.

Moondani Balluk Indigenous Academic Unit
Friends of Iramoo
Cairnlea Conservation Reserves Committee of Management
Melbourne Water
Landcare Australia
Nursery
Iramoo Native Plant Nursery propagates indigenous species from locally collected seed — supplying restoration projects, schools, gardens and councils across Melbourne's west.
What we grow
Tubestock and advanced plants of grasses, lilies, daisies, orchids and shrubs native to the basalt plains. All seed is provenance-tracked from the Iramoo grassland and surrounding remnants.
